study: UK House of Commons 2024 election official constituency-level results
unit: UK constituency; up to 650, 4 nations and English regions
prespecified_exclusions: Only missing electorate/turnout or no winner-runner candidate votes for computation; report exclusions and special Speaker/NI observations; don't discard by result
classification: All cycles exploratory until independently replicated; contemporaneous margins and vote shares are post-election, cannot be used in genuine pre-election prediction.
A: Is constituency turnout higher in electorally competitive seats, using the realized winner–runner-up margin as descriptive competition indicator, or is the association negligible/reversed?

B.H1: Turnout decreases as final margin percent increases: Spearman rho < -0.1
B.Halt: Positive/curvilinear pattern due strong safe-seat mobilization or social geography.

C: Pre-specify winner–runner-up margin (votes/electorate or share of valid vote, choose valid vote denominator if derivable), turnout percentage, Pearson, Spearman, turnout difference in equal-sized quartiles and a quadratic check; report zero and positive results.
F: Margin is measured after election and endogenous to turnout; cross-sectional descriptive not anticipatory or causal.
G: One election, need external election/time for generalizability.
J: Persist all results even reversed direction.
